The City Council wants to expand the Fair Fares program so more than 1 million eligible New Yorkers would be able to ride Big Apple subways and buses all on the government’s dime.

Lower-income households often spend a disproportionate share of their income on transportation and have the least flexibility to absorb regular fare increases. “New Jersey is rightly investing billions of dollars to modernize and improve NJ TRANSIT, but affordability has to be part of that conversation,” said Zoe Baldwin, Vice President for State Programs at Regional Plan Association. ​“A transit system only provides access to opportunity if people can afford to ride it. Fair Fares would provide meaningful relief to New Jerseyans who need it most while helping ensure that our public investment in transit serves everyone.”
The coalition will work with transit riders, community organizations, policymakers, and advocates across the state to build support for a Fair Fares program and ensure that the experiences of riders are central to its design. ​“Providing affordable transportation to working-class New Jerseyans is crucial for households across the state,” said Johan Andrade, President of Hudson County Complete Streets. ​“Trenton should be doing everything possible to ensure NJ TRANSIT is available for everyone that needs it, and Fair Fares NJ is a big step towards achieving that.”
